detail: STROKE CENTER DESIGNATION AT MY PROGRAM'S NAMESAKE HOSPITAL. Dell Med's own Vascular Neurology Fellowship page describes Ascension Seton Medical Center Austin as a '447-bed' facility that is a 'primary plus thrombectomy-capable stroke center with robust cardiology services', reserving 'Comprehensive Stroke Center' and 'Level 1 trauma center' for the 211-bed Dell Seton Medical Center. Ascension's own hospital page for Ascension Seton Medical Center Austin calls it a 'Comprehensive Level 1 Stroke Center' with the American Heart Association 'Stroke Gold Plus, Target Stroke Honor Roll' award. A third source reports 391 beds and Joint Commission comprehensive stroke certification. The most likely reconciliation is that Texas operates a state stroke-facility designation ('Level I Comprehensive') that is distinct from Joint Commission Comprehensive Stroke Center certification, and that the two pages are quoting different schemes; the bed discrepancy (447 vs 391) may reflect licensed versus staffed beds. I have not resolved it. This matters for the twin-program question because it is one of the few genuine clinical differences between the two named sites: Dell Seton is the region's Comprehensive Stroke Center and holds the Level IV epilepsy monitoring unit and Austin's first neuro-ICU, while Ascension Seton Medical Center Austin is the larger general hospital with the stronger cardiology and obstetric case mix.

detail: PROGRAM TYPE - THE CENTRAL CONFLICT. NRMP's own Program Results 2022-2026 lists UT Tyler Neurology under exactly one code, 3626180R0, for both appointment years it has participated in (2025 and 2026). NRMP defines an 'R' code as a Physician position that 'begins in the year of the Match', is 'reserved for physicians with prior graduate medical education', and explicitly states 'Physician positions are not available to senior medical students.' FREIDA's 2026 program survey, completed by the program itself and received 2026-06-12, instead ticks field_pgy2_pos_type_advanced = true with field_pgy2_pos_type_reserved = false, which would make it an 'A' code that a senior student CAN match. The program's own webpage uses the word 'advanced' in plain English ('The program is currently an advanced one and will accept residents starting in the PGY-2 year') without naming an NRMP code. The 2027-appointment-year code is not yet published anywhere. This conflict decides whether Alejandra is eligible to apply at all in her graduating cycle and cannot be resolved from published sources; it must be settled by direct enquiry to the program.

detail: PROGRAM NAME VERSUS INSTITUTIONAL HANDBOOK — THE CENTRAL AFFILIATION CONFLICT. The ACGME/FREIDA program name, the FREIDA sponsoring-institution name, and the program's own public page all read 'Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Baylor College of Medicine (Temple)'. But the House Staff Handbook that BSW Temple's own GME page links as the governing policy document, revised March 2024, opens with: 'The handbook serves as a general reference for information pertaining to The Texas A&M Health Science Center College of Medicine - Baylor Scott & White Graduate Medical Education Programs. So the institution's current, self-declared-superseding policy document still carries the OLD Texas A&M co-branding while every other current artefact carries the Baylor College of Medicine name. Resolution by primary evidence: the Baylor College of Medicine name is the CURRENT and CORRECT one. Baylor Scott & White Health and Baylor College of Medicine announced a new 20-year affiliation on 17 November 2020 anchored by 'a progressive four-year regional medical school campus in Temple, Texas', with an inaugural class of 40 students anticipated in Autumn 2023 and campus growth of 40 students a year over four years, overseen by the BCM School of Medicine Dean with students 'educated by Baylor College of Medicine faculty members' and 'trained in the state-of-the-art facilities at Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Temple'. The same release describes Texas A&M's relationship with BSWH as CONTINUING BUT RELOCATED — a major expansion of the Texas A&M Health DALLAS campus, with the release listing Texas A&M College of Medicine campuses as Bryan/College Station, Houston and Austin/Round Rock,

FREIDA reports field_usmle_step_1_required = false and field_usmle_step_2_required = false in BOTH the 2025 and 2026 survey cycles, and field_usmle_step1_req_int = false and field_usmle_step2_req_int = false. The program's own pages state 'Passing USMLE Step 1 or COMLEX Level 1 score to apply' and 'A passing Step 2 or COMLEX 2 score is required to be ranked.' The FREIDA booleans appear to encode whether a minimum SCORE is required rather than whether a PASS is required; reading them as 'Step 1 and Step 2 are not required' would be a serious error. Resolved in favour of the program pages, with the FREIDA values preserved here.

program_name: Florida Atlantic University Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine Program — Neurology
detail: PARTICIPATING SITE LIST. FREIDA's participating institutions for this program are Boca Raton Regional Hospital, Delray Medical Center, Pediatric Neurologists of Palm Beach Gardens and FAU Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine. The program's own teaching-hospitals page names Boca Raton Regional Hospital, Delray Medical Center and St. Mary's Medical Center — and identifies St. Mary's, not Pediatric Neurologists of Palm Beach Gardens, as the site of the pediatric neurology requirement. Meanwhile the program's faculty page lists three physicians under the heading 'Pediatric Neurologists of Palm Beach'. The most coherent reading is that the pediatric neurology rotation involves both a Tenet hospital site (St. Mary's) and a named pediatric neurology practice group, and that FREIDA and the program page each list only part of that arrangement. Both lists preserved; neither discarded.

program_name: Florida Atlantic University Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine Program — Neurology
detail: FAU GME CONSORTIUM VERSUS NEUROLOGY TEACHING SITES. FAU's GME page states the FAU Consortium for Graduate Medical Education consists of Boca Raton Regional Hospital, Bethesda Hospital East, Delray Medical Center, St. Mary's Medical Center and West Boca Medical Center. The neurology residency's own teaching-hospitals page lists only BRRH, Delray and St. Mary's. Bethesda Hospital East and West Boca Medical Center are therefore consortium members that this neurology residency does not use — a distinction that matters because the orchestrator's tasking raised Bethesda Hospital East as a candidate neurology site. The West Palm Beach VA Medical Center appears in neither list and is not a site for this program.

program_name: Larkin Community Hospital Palm Springs Campus Program
detail: THE TWO-LARKIN IDENTITY QUESTION - ESTABLISHED, WITH RESIDUALS NAMED. This ticket's defining hazard was whether ACGME 1801100158 ('Larkin Community Hospital Palm Springs Campus Program', Hialeah) and ACGME 1801100156 ('Larkin Community Hospital Program', South Miami) are two real programs or one department under two accreditations. WHAT I ESTABLISHED, on seven independent lines of evidence: they are TWO SEPARATE ACCREDITATIONS WITH SEPARATE SPONSORING INSTITUTIONS, SEPARATE COMPLEMENTS, SEPARATE NRMP CODES, SEPARATE PROGRAM DIRECTORS, SEPARATE COORDINATORS, SEPARATE FACULTY ROSTERS, SEPARATE RESIDENT ROSTERS, SEPARATE CURRICULA AND LARGELY SEPARATE CLINICAL NETWORKS - administered by one shared Larkin Health System GME office. The decisive item is the Texas-style one the ticket asked for: TWO LIVE NRMP PROGRAM CODES PUBLISHED SIDE BY SIDE in NRMP's own directory - 2238180C0 (institution code 2238, Hialeah, ACGME 1801100158, PD Kester Nedd, Active) and 1481180C0 (institution code 1481, South Miami, ACGME 1801100156, PD Wilson Cueva, Active). Different institution codes AND different program codes. Corroborated by: separate field_sponsor_institution values in FREIDA's relationship graph (Larkin Community Hospital Palm Springs Campus, institution 119718, versus Larkin Community Hospital, institution 119101); separate FREIDA program nodes created 2021-02-12 and 2019-10-18; two independently completed 2026 surveys received 2026-07-21 and 2026-06-16 that disagree on DO share, IMG share, moonlighting, YOG limit and interview volume; two fully parallel six-page sets on the shared GME site ('-psc' suffixed versus unsuffixed); Larkin's own institutional program list showing Neurology exactly once under each campus; and a near-disjoint participating-site network with only North Sh

program_name: Larkin Community Hospital Palm Springs Campus Program
detail: STEP 2 CK TIMING - AN INTERNAL FREIDA CONTRADICTION, PRESERVED. Within the single survey record received 2026-07-21, field_usmle_us_md_pass_ck, field_usmle_img_pass_ck and field_comlex_do_pass_ce are all TRUE and are rendered on FREIDA's public page under the heading 'Medical Exam Licensing Requirements for Interview Consideration', while field_usmle_step2_req_int and field_usmle_step1_req_int are both FALSE. On a plain reading of the field names these contradict each other. I weighted the rendered public page - which is what an applicant actually sees, and which explicitly attaches the requirement to interview consideration - and coded REQUIRES_STEP2_BEFORE_INTERVIEW at MEDIUM confidence, but both readings are preserved. A third field pair (field_usmle_step_1_required / field_usmle_step_2_required, both false) renders as the single line 'Requires the USMLE Step 1 and/or Step 2 CK | No' positioned after the DO block and is the DO-USMLE question (field_do_usmle_req_ind=false); misreading that line as a general Step 2 waiver is the specific trap here, and it is a trap the registry fell into by capturing only the Step 1 rows of that block. The program's own Application Process page publishes no examination requirement at all and so neither corroborates nor contradicts FREIDA.

detail: CORE FACULTY COUNT - a five-fold disagreement between consecutive survey cycles. 2025-07-16 cycle: 5 physician faculty, 2 non-physician faculty, faculty-to-resident ratio 0.60:1. 2026-07-21 cycle: field_total_physician = 1, field_total_non_physician = 0, field_ratio_ft_faculty = '0.10'. No published faculty roster exists to arbitrate. Note this is the mirror image of the Texas null-sentinel-as-zero defect: here the NEWER figure is the suspect one.

program_name: Palmetto General Hospital Program
detail: PROGRAM DIRECTOR AND FELLOWSHIP DIRECTOR APPEAR ON ANOTHER INSTITUTION'S FACULTY ROSTER. Larkin Community Hospital's GME site lists 'Ariol Labrada, M.D.' and 'Roberto Sanchez, M.D.' under the heading 'CURRENT DEPARTMENT MEMBERS' of the Larkin neurology department, while FREIDA's survey received 2026-07-21 lists the same two men as Palmetto General's neurology program director and vascular neurology fellowship director, with hsahospitals.com institutional e-mail addresses. I verified that neither man is Larkin's program director (Larkin Palm Springs Campus: Kester Nedd DO; Larkin South Miami: Wilson Cueva MD), so a title collision is not the explanation. Concurrent hospital appointment is the most probable reconciliation and is ordinary in South Florida community neurology; a departure from Palmetto cannot be excluded from public evidence, though the July 2026 FREIDA survey with an HSA address argues against it. Personal training histories were taken from the Larkin page because a person's training is a property of the person; no Larkin program, curriculum, roster, faculty-count, subspecialty or designation content was imported.

program_name: Palmetto General Hospital Program
detail: COMPREHENSIVE STROKE CENTER CERTIFICATION - claimed but not verifiable against the awarding body. The hospital's neurology page states verbatim that it 'is a Comprehensive Stroke Center' and 'has earned recognition from The Joint Commission and the American Heart Association (AHA)/American Stroke Association (ASA) as meeting The Joint Commission's standards for Comprehensive Stroke Center Certification', adding 'This designation makes Palmetto General Hospital one of 110 hospitals in the nation - one of four in Florida - to receive this accreditation.' The '110 hospitals nationally / four in Florida' figures are characteristic of mid-2010s Tenet-era copy and are almost certainly stale, since far more than 110 US hospitals now hold that certification. The Joint Commission's own Quality Check directory returned HTTP 403 to both its search page and its API, so the certification's CURRENT status could not be checked against the awarding body as contamination guard 8 requires. The claim is quoted and attributed, flagged as unverified against the awarding body, and not restated as a present-tense fact by this dossier.

program_name: Palmetto General Hospital Program
detail: PROGRAM ACCREDITATION STATUS - unknown, and third-party assertions quarantined. The program's own 2020 FAQ stated 'The program has initial accreditation through the ACGME' and 'We are currently accepting applications through ERAS as an ACGME initial-accredited program' - a 2020 statement about a program founded around 2018. Six years on, a program that has completed multiple cohorts would ordinarily hold Continued Accreditation, but I cannot verify that: ACGME's public program search is reCAPTCHA-gated and was not bypassed, and the public detail endpoint 302-redirects to 'No Results Found' because it keys on an internal ADS identifier rather than the public ACGME ID. Several quarantined aggregators assert accreditation statuses for Palmetto General programs; one such claim of 'Continued' accreditation that surfaced in search related to the SIBLING INTERNAL MEDICINE program 1401100953, not to this program, and is doubly rejected - once as an aggregator accreditation claim and once as cross-program contamination. Current accreditation status for 1801100160 is UNAVAILABLE_DUE_TO_ACCESS_BOUNDARY.

The Parkinson's Foundation's own Florida Chapter page currently names 'University of South Florida Parkinson's Disease and Movement Disorders' as one of three Florida Parkinson's Foundation Centers of Excellence. The underlying designation is live at the awarding body; USF's own wording is stale. Preserved because a reader checking USF's phrase against the Foundation's current programme names would not find a match and might wrongly conclude the designation had lapsed.

program_name: University of South Florida Morsani Program - Adult Neurology Residency
detail: NRMP R-POSITION FOOTNOTE, AS AN EVIDENCE NOTE RATHER THAN A PROGRAM CONFLICT - the research contract records an unreconciled dispute about whether NRMP publishes a footnote asserting that physician positions are closed to students still in medical school. That disputed wording is deliberately NOT reproduced verbatim anywhere in this dossier, so it cannot be extracted downstream as if it were NRMP's language. A direct case-insensitive search of the three NRMP Program Results PDFs downloaded in this session (2017-2021, 2021-2025 and 2022-2026) returned ZERO occurrences of the phrase 'senior medical student' in any of them. This corroborates the Florida adversarial reviewer rather than the Texas agent. The phrase is therefore not quoted anywhere in this dossier. NRMP's actual and verifiable wording, which IS present, is: 'Reserved Positions ("R"): PGY-2 positions in specialty programs that begin in the year of the Match and are reserved for physicians with prior graduate medical education. These positions are also known as "Physician Positions".' The substantive conclusion is unchanged: a June 2027 graduate with no prior graduate medical education cannot take an R position.

program_name: Cleveland Clinic Foundation/Florida Weston Program (self-described as the Cleveland Clinic Florida Neurology Residency Program)
detail: PROGRAM DIRECTOR TITLE. Efrain D. Salgado, MD's Cleveland Clinic provider biography states verbatim 'Efrain D Salgado, MD, is Director of the Neurology Residency Training Program at Cleveland Clinic Florida and Director of the Cleveland Clinic Florida Stroke Center and Neurosonology Laboratory.' Three independent 2026-dated sources instead name Mansour Afshani, MD as (Interim) Program Director and list Salgado only as 'Staff': the program page's own Our Team list and signed welcome letter, the FREIDA field_program_director paragraph attached to the survey received 2026-06-15, and the NRMP Main Residency Match Program Directory entries for both neurology codes. The most probable explanation is an un-updated provider biography for a long-serving former director, corroborated by two published alumni testimonials from the Class of 2018 that describe Salgado in a directorial mentoring role. Not resolved; both preserved. Practical consequence: correspondence should be addressed to Afshani as interim director via coordinator Belinda Ortiz, while Salgado should be understood as the program's senior stroke figure, its former director, and a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate.

program_name: Cleveland Clinic Foundation/Florida Weston Program (self-described as the Cleveland Clinic Florida Neurology Residency Program)
detail: STEP 1 AND STEP 2 'REQUIRED' FLAGS. The FREIDA 2026 survey (received 2026-06-15) sets field_usmle_step_1_required = false, field_usmle_step_2_required = false, field_usmle_step1_req_int = false, field_usmle_step2_req_int = false, field_comlex_lvl1_req_int = false and field_comlex_lvl2_req_int = false. The registry snapshot, drawn from the 2025-06-11 survey, records all of 'US MD Step 1 Required: Yes', 'US MD Step 2 Required: Yes', 'IMG Step 1 Required: Yes', 'IMG Step 2 Required: Yes', 'DO Step 1/2 Required: Yes' and 'DO COMLEX Level 1/2 Required: Yes'. Meanwhile the program's own page states an applicant without a Step 2 score report uploaded by the rank-list deadline 'will not be ranked'. The three cannot all be true on one reading. The most coherent reading is that FREIDA's 'required' fields encode a required minimum SCORE rather than a required score REPORT, which would make the 2026 false values consistent with the program's '>220 is suggested' language. Not resolved. The program page is treated as operative for both the requirement and the timing.

program_name: Cleveland Clinic Foundation/Florida Weston Program (self-described as the Cleveland Clinic Florida Neurology Residency Program)
detail: STEP 2 TIMING, INTERNAL TO THE PROGRAM'S OWN PAGE. The How to Apply preamble ('You must complete all components of the ERAS Application for your application to be considered complete and to be reviewed by the Selection Committee') lists the Step 2 transcript among the components, implying a pre-review requirement. The immediately following bullet sets the deadline at rank-list submission and its parenthetical, 'assuming you were invited for an interview', presupposes interviewing applicants with no Step 2 score uploaded. The specific rule is taken as operative and the tension is recorded, not erased.

program_name: Cleveland Clinic Foundation/Florida Weston Program (self-described as the Cleveland Clinic Florida Neurology Residency Program)
detail: PRELIMINARY POSITIONS. The registry records 'Offers Preliminary Positions: Yes' while FREIDA 2026 reports field_offers_preliminary_positio = false for the neurology program — yet field_pgy1_pos_type_prelim = true and field_coordinated_pgy1_pos = true, and the program page describes dedicated preliminary positions at length. Resolved as a semantic mismatch rather than a factual conflict: the NEUROLOGY program does not itself offer preliminary positions; the dedicated preliminary year is a track inside the Cleveland Clinic Florida INTERNAL MEDICINE program (NRMP 1383140P0, ACGME 1401121528), coordinated with the neurology match. Both values are defensible against different questions and both are recorded.

program_name: Cleveland Clinic Foundation/Florida Weston Program (self-described as the Cleveland Clinic Florida Neurology Residency Program)
detail: PARKINSON'S FOUNDATION DESIGNATION SCOPE AND COUNT. The Cleveland Clinic Florida Parkinson's page states 'Cleveland Clinic Weston Hospital receiving a Center of Excellence designation by the Parkinson's Foundation, one of only 47 centers worldwide with this designation.' Cleveland Clinic Florida's own Awards page states the more precise 'Center of Excellence (Multi-Site Award)'. The Parkinson's Foundation's own listing, updated April 2026, states 59 Centers of Excellence worldwide (46 U.S., 13 international) and names no Cleveland Clinic Florida or Weston site; its two Cleveland Clinic entries are in Nevada and Ohio, and its three Florida entries are UF Fixel, University of Miami and USF. Both the scope ('Weston Hospital receiving a designation' vs a multi-site award covering Weston as one site) and the count ('47 worldwide' vs 59) conflict. All three sources preserved.
